definitions.explanation: The late night hours, typically from around midnight to early morning when most people are asleep.

examples.english: I woke up in the middle of the night.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}に{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}りました。
examples.english: The phone rang in the middle of the night.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}まで{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.english: I studied until the middle of the night.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}に{外|そと}で{大|おお}きな{音|おと}がして、びっくりしました。
examples.english: I was startled by a loud noise outside in the middle of the night.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}の{二時|にじ}ごろに{赤|あか}ちゃんが{泣|な}き{出|だ}したので、{母|はは}は{起|お}きてミルクをあげました。
examples.english: The baby started crying around 2 AM, so the mother got up and gave milk.

notes: {夜中|よなか} refers to the deep night hours when most people are sleeping. It's later than {夜|よる} (night) and typically suggests the hours around and after midnight. Use {夜中|よなか}に for 'in the middle of the night' and {夜中|よなか}まで for 'until the middle of the night.'
